stem: A toy car travels on a circular track at a constant speed of $0.50\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. It passes a point on the track at time $t=0$ and takes $40\ \mathrm{s}$ to travel once around the track. The magnitude of the average velocity of the car between $t=0$ and $t=20\ \mathrm{s}$ is $v_{20}$. The magnitude of the average velocity between $t=0$ and $t=40\ \mathrm{s}$ is $v_{40}$. What are $v_{20}$ and $v_{40}$, in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$?
The graph shows the variation with time of the acceleration of a car. What must the shaded area under the graph represent?

options.A: the average velocity of the car
options.B: the change in velocity of the car
options.C: the final velocity of the car
options.D: the initial velocity of the car

stem: A stone is thrown vertically upwards from a point X at time $t=0$. The variation with time $t$ of the velocity $v$ of the stone is shown. What is the displacement of the stone from point X at time $t=3.0\ \mathrm{s}$?

The graph shows the variation with time $t$ of the velocity of a vehicle moving in a straight line. The vehicle, moving at $4.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, begins to accelerate at time $t=0$. What is the vehicle's acceleration at time $t=3.0\ \mathrm{s}$?

A train, initially at rest at a station, has a uniform acceleration of $0.20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it reaches a speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. It travels for a time at this constant speed and then has a uniform deceleration of $0.40\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it comes to rest at the next station. The distance between the two stations is $3000\ \mathrm{m}$. What is the time taken by the train to travel between the two stations?

A ball is thrown vertically upwards from ground level and reaches a maximum height of $12.7\ \mathrm{m}$ before falling back to ground level. Assume that air resistance is negligible. What is the total time for which the ball is in the air?

The time taken for an object to fall from rest through a certain distance on Mars is $T_\mathrm{M}$. The time taken for the same object to fall from rest through the same distance on Earth is $T_\mathrm{E}$. The acceleration of free fall on Mars is $3.71\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Assume that air resistance is negligible on both Earth and Mars. What is the ratio $T_\mathrm{M}/T_\mathrm{E}$?

A steel ball is dropped from rest from a height $h$ above the ground. The ball hits the ground after a time $t$. This is repeated for a number of different heights. The graph shows the variation of $h$ with $t^2$ for the ball, a straight line through the origin. The gradient of the graph is $G$. Which expression gives the acceleration of the ball?

An astronaut on the Moon, where there is no air resistance, throws a ball. The ball's initial velocity has a vertical component of $8.00\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and a horizontal component of $4.00\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The acceleration of free fall on the Moon is $1.62\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. What is the speed of the ball $9.00\ \mathrm{s}$ after being thrown?

A ball is thrown horizontally with a speed of $10.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ above horizontal ground. The ball hits the ground after a time of $3.0\ \mathrm{s}$. Air resistance is negligible. What is the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground?

A projectile is launched at an angle above horizontal ground and travels through the air. The projectile reaches its maximum height at position X. Assume that no upthrust acts on the projectile. Which diagram shows the directions of the force or forces acting on the projectile at position X?

A goods train passes through a station at a steady speed of $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at time $t=0$. An express train is at rest at the station. The express train leaves the station with a uniform acceleration of $0.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ just as the goods train goes past. Both trains move in the same direction on straight, parallel tracks. At which time $t$ does the express train overtake the goods train?
A car travels at a constant speed along a semicircular road of radius 75 m, from one end of a diameter to the other, in 20 s. Calculate the magnitude of the average velocity of the car.
A car moves round a roundabout at a constant speed of $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Its velocity is changing because its direction is changing, so it is accelerating.
options.B: Its acceleration is zero because its speed is constant.
options.C: Its velocity is constant because its speed is constant.
options.D: Its displacement from its starting point increases at a constant rate.

stem: A ball travelling at 15 m s$^{-1}$ towards a wall rebounds along the same line at 9 m s$^{-1}$. It is in contact with the wall for 5 ms. Calculate the magnitude of the average acceleration of the ball during the contact.
For an object moving in a straight line, which row shows what the gradient and the area under a velocity-time graph represent?

A ball is thrown vertically upwards, rises, and falls back to the ground, air resistance being negligible. Taking upwards as positive, which describes the velocity-time graph from launch to the moment before landing?

options.A: one straight line with a positive gradient
options.B: one straight line with a negative gradient, crossing the time axis at the highest point
options.C: a curve with zero gradient at the highest point
options.D: a straight line falling to zero and then rising again to positive values

stem: The velocity of a trolley changes uniformly from 5 m s$^{-1}$ to 18 m s$^{-1}$ in 2 s, so its velocity-time graph is a straight line. Determine the acceleration of the trolley.

The velocity-time graph of a cyclist is a horizontal line at 12 m s$^{-1}$ for 8 s, followed by a straight line falling uniformly to zero over a further 3 s. Determine the total displacement of the cyclist.

The velocity of an object moving along a straight line changes uniformly from 10 m s$^{-1}$ in one direction at $t=0$ to 4 m s$^{-1}$ in the opposite direction at $t=4$ s. Determine its displacement from its starting point at $t=4$ s, in the direction of the initial velocity.
The displacement-time graph of a runner is a straight line passing through the points (3 s, 2 m) and (8 s, 36 m). Determine the velocity of the runner.
The displacement-time graph for an object is a curve whose gradient increases steadily with time. What does this show?

options.A: The velocity of the object is decreasing.
options.B: The object moves with constant velocity.
options.C: The velocity of the object is increasing.

stem: The displacement-time graph for an object is a straight line sloping downwards from the top left to the bottom right. What does this show?

options.A: The object is moving with constant velocity in the negative direction.
options.C: The object is moving with constant velocity in the positive direction.
options.D: The object is moving with constant acceleration in the negative direction.

stem: A car moving in the positive direction slows uniformly from $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ to $4.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in $2.0\ \mathrm{s}$. Determine its acceleration.
The equation $s=\tfrac12(u+v)t$ uses $\tfrac12(u+v)$ as the average velocity. Why is this valid only for uniform acceleration?

options.A: Uniform acceleration means the velocity is constant, so $u=v$.
options.B: Uniform acceleration means the velocity changes at a constant rate, so the average velocity is halfway between $u$ and $v$.
options.C: Uniform acceleration means the acceleration equals $9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
options.D: Uniform acceleration means the object is moving in a straight line, whatever the acceleration.

stem: A body has uniform acceleration. Its velocity-time graph is a straight line from $u$ at $t=0$ to $v$ at time $t$. Which expression gives the area under the graph, the displacement?
For uniform acceleration $a$, use $v=u+at$ and $s=\tfrac12(u+v)t$ to eliminate $t$ and write $v^2$ in terms of $u$, $a$ and $s$.

A car accelerates uniformly. Its initial velocity, final velocity and displacement are known and its acceleration is required. Which equation should be used, because the time is neither given nor asked for?
A stone is dropped from rest from a bridge 45 m above a river. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the river.
A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 20 m s$^{-1}$ from ground level. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the maximum height reached by the ball.
A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 20 m s$^{-1}$ from ground level and returns to ground level. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the total time for which the ball is in the air.
A car travelling at 25 m s$^{-1}$ brakes with uniform deceleration and stops in a distance of 60 m. Calculate the magnitude of the deceleration.
A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Air resistance is negligible. Which row gives the velocity and acceleration of the ball at its highest point?

In a free-fall experiment a steel ball is released from rest at different heights $h$ and the time $t$ of fall is measured. The graph of $h$ against $t^2$ is a straight line through the origin with gradient 4.90 m s$^{-2}$. Determine the acceleration of free fall.
A steel ball is released from rest and falls a height $h$ in time $t$. Which graph gives a straight line whose gradient can be used to find the acceleration of free fall?
In a free-fall experiment a steel ball released from rest falls a distance of 2.5 m in a time of 0.71 s. Calculate the acceleration of free fall.
A ball is kicked horizontally at 12 m s$^{-1}$ from the top of a cliff 80 m high. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the horizontal distance from the foot of the cliff to where the ball lands.
A ball is kicked from level ground at 20 m s$^{-1}$ at 60$^\circ$ above the horizontal. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the maximum height reached by the ball.
Ball A is dropped from rest from the top of a tower. At the same instant ball B is fired horizontally from the same point with a large speed. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement is correct?

options.A: They land at the same time because their vertical motions are identical.
options.B: A lands first because B has further to travel.
options.C: B lands first because it has a horizontal velocity as well.
options.D: Which lands first depends on the horizontal speed of B.

stem: A runner goes $240\ \mathrm{m}$ due east then $70\ \mathrm{m}$ due north in $25\ \mathrm{s}$. Determine the magnitude of the average velocity.
A lift starts from rest, accelerates uniformly at $2.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $4.0\ \mathrm{s}$, then moves at constant velocity. Determine its constant speed.
The velocity of a trolley changes uniformly from $+8.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t=0$ to $-2.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t=5.0\ \mathrm{s}$. Determine its displacement at $t=5.0\ \mathrm{s}$.

A tangent to a displacement-time curve at $t=2.0\ \mathrm{s}$ passes through $(1.0\ \mathrm{s},\ 0\ \mathrm{m})$ and $(3.0\ \mathrm{s},\ 8.0\ \mathrm{m})$. Determine the velocity at $t=2.0\ \mathrm{s}$.
A car's velocity-time graph is a straight line from $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t=2.0\ \mathrm{s}$ to $5.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at $t=8.0\ \mathrm{s}$. Determine its acceleration.
A body has $u=3.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and uniform acceleration $2.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $5.0\ \mathrm{s}$. Determine its displacement.
A stone is thrown vertically upwards at $15\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from ground level. Determine the maximum height. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
A graph of $h$ against $t^2$ is a straight line through the origin passing through $(0.250\ \mathrm{s^2},\ 1.20\ \mathrm{m})$. Determine the acceleration of free fall.
